Putin agrees to cooperate with Pope Leo’s plea for aid for Ukrainian town

Reuters

16 October, 2026 11:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Joshua McElwee VATICAN CITY, Oct 16 (Reuters) – President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo he had agreed to cooperate after the pontiff asked him on Friday to help get vital supplies into the Russian-controlled Ukrainian town of Oleshky, the Kremlin said.

Leo phoned Putin and asked him to arrange a ceasefire to let aid and food into the town, taken by Russian forces in February 2022, the Vatican said. Residents have reported a deepening food crisis.

Leo expressed “deep concern” over the humanitarian situation there, the Vatican added. Russia and Ukraine accuse each other of blocking supplies to the town, which Ukrainian forces want to retake.

Show Full Article

“The Vatican’s intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town’s population and to organise vital supplies has been supported,” the Kremlin said in a statement. It did not mention a ceasefire.

“It has been agreed to cooperate on this matter,” it added.

Leo and Putin are known to have spoken once previously, in June 2025. The pope also reaffirmed the Holy See’s commitment to any initiatives for peace, the Vatican said.

The pope, 71, is recovering at Rome’s Gemelli hospital after surgery for lung cancer. The Vatican said earlier on Friday that he is showing steady improvement and is able to work and do normal daily activities. The Kremlin said Putin had wished Leo a speedy and full recovery.

The Vatican’s Secretary of State, Cardinal Pietro Parolin, told reporters after the call that it had been Leo’s initiative. The pope, he said, wanted “to plead the cause of this besieged city”.

Russia has acknowledged critical problems with food and medical supplies in Oleshky and said its military was working to resolve them. It blamed Ukraine for the crisis, saying it was obstructing those supplies from getting to the town. Ukraine has said it is Russia which is thwarting food deliveries.

Oleshky, in Ukraine’s Kherson region, had a pre-war population of some 24,000, and is still home to around 1,700 residents, including 47 children, according to Danielle Bell, head of the UN Human Rights Monitoring Mission in Ukraine.

(Reporting by Joshua McElwee; Additional reporting by Moscow buro; Editing by Andrew Heavensediting by Gianluca Semeraro and David Gregorio)

Kremlin says Putin told Pope Leo he backs Vatican idea to help civilians in Oleshky

Reuters

16 October, 2026 10:00 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

MOSCOW, Oct 16 (Reuters) – Russian President Vladimir Putin told Pope Leo in a phone call on Friday that he supported a Vatican initiative to help deliver supplies to civilians in the Russian-controlled town of Oleshky in southern Ukraine and was ready to cooperate on the matter.

The Vatican said earlier on Friday that Leo had urged Putin to agree to a truce to allow the entry of first aid and food supplies into the town and to permit a voluntary evacuation of the civilian population.

Russia and Ukraine both accuse each other of blocking supplies to the population of the town which Ukrainian forces want to retake.

Show Full Article

“The Vatican’s intention to help create the conditions necessary to ensure the safety of the town’s population and to organise vital supplies has been supported,” the Kremlin said in a statement.

“It has been agreed to cooperate on this matter.”

(Reporting by ReutersEditing by Andrew Osborn )

Trudy forecast to near Mexico’s Pacific coast as major hurricane through the weekend

Reuters

16 October, 2026 09:30 pm IST

Facebook

Twitter

WhatsApp

Linkedin

(c) Copyright Thomson Reuters 2026

Follow Us :

Text Size: A- A+

-->

By Aida Pelaez-Fernandez MEXICO CITY; Oct 16 (Reuters) – Hurricane Trudy rapidly intensified on Friday, carrying maximum winds near 120 mph (195 kph), and is expected to approach Mexico’s Pacific coast as a major storm during the weekend.

Additional strengthening is still forecast before Trudy nears the coast of Jalisco and Colima states late on Saturday as a life-threatening major hurricane, Mexican authorities and the US-based National Hurricane Center warned.

It is not expected to make landfall but will remain very close to the coast, about 60 to 65 km away, and any change in its path closer to shore will increase the severity of its impact, the head of Mexico’s weather agency Fabian Vazquez said at a press conference.

Show Full Article

“Everyone in this region needs to be very careful and stay alert over the weekend,” he added.

Mexico’s civil protection agency asked residents to start preparations for the storm’s arrival by securing doors and windows, and removing objects that could be thrown around by the strong winds.

“Trudy has the potential to even reach Category 4 or 5 intensity,” said Alex DaSilva, a hurricane meteorologist at private forecaster AccuWeather.

Located about 235 miles (380 km) southwest of resort city Acapulco, the storm is expected to produce up to 15 inches (38 cm) of rain in the states of Michoacan, Colima and Jalisco, increasing the risk of life-threatening flooding and landslides, according to the NHC.

HARD-HIT PACIFIC COAST

The hurricane will strike Mexico’s Pacific coast, a region that has already been battered in recent weeks by storms that left several dead and caused severe flooding.

“The most critical conditions will start on Saturday, with very severe winds and waves along the coast, in an area that has already been affected for several weeks,” Vazquez said.

Tropical Storm Simon continues to weaken farther northwest offshore, after dropping heavy rain along the coast earlier as a hurricane.

Last week, tropical storm Rachel hit the Baja California peninsula damaging 1,500 homes, according to Mexican President Claudia Sheinbaum.

(Reporting by Aida Pelaez-Fernandez, Additional reporting by Raul Cortes; Editing by Toby Chopra)
